title: Inverse image comparison for free module sheaves
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D$ be small sites [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $f:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism], so that $f^{-1}:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal D)$ is left adjoint to $f_*$ and preserves finite limits. Let $\mathcal B$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $\mathcal C$; give $f^{-1}\mathcal B$ the ring operations obtained by applying $f^{-1}$ to those of $\mathcal B$ through the finite-product comparisons, and likewise make $f^{-1}$ of a $\mathcal B$-module sheaf [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] an $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaf. For a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O$ and a sheaf of sets $\mathcal F$ on a site, the free $\mathcal O$-module sheaf $\mathcal O[\mathcal F]$ is the module sheafification [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification] (in particular a sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]) of the presheaf of $\mathcal O$-modules $U\mapsto\mathcal O(U)[\mathcal F(U)]$, the free $\mathcal O(U)$-module with basis $\{[s]:s\in\mathcal F(U)\}$ [def-weil-pbc-free-module], with restrictions $\sum a_s[s]\mapsto\sum a_s|_V[s|_V]$; its generator map $\mathcal F\to\mathcal O[\mathcal F]$ (as sheaves of sets) is induced by $s\mapsto[s]$. Then for every sheaf of sets $\mathcal E$ on $\mathcal C$ there is a canonical isomorphism of $f^{-1}\mathcal B$-module sheaves $f^{-1}(\mathcal B[\mathcal E])\xrightarrow{\sim}(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[f^{-1}\mathcal E]$ which carries $f^{-1}$ of the generator map of $\mathcal B[\mathcal E]$ to the generator map of $(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[f^{-1}\mathcal E]$. It is natural in $\mathcal E$ and in ring-sheaf maps $\mathcal B\to\mathcal B_1$. It is compatible with finite products: for a finite family $(\mathcal E_i)$ and $\mathcal E=\prod_i\mathcal E_i$, its composite with the map of free modules induced by the comparison $\lambda:f^{-1}\prod_i\mathcal E_i\cong\prod_if^{-1}\mathcal E_i$ carries $f^{-1}$ of the generator map to the generator map of $(f^{-1}\mathcal B)[\prod_if^{-1}\mathcal E_i]$ composed with $\lambda$. For the identity geometric morphism it is the identity, and for composable geometric morphisms the comparison of the composite equals the composite of the two comparisons.

proof.text: Put $L=f^{-1}$ and let $i:E\to|B[E]|$, $j:LE\to|(LB)[LE]|$ be the generator maps. The transported Hom bijection gives $L(B[E])$ the free universal property on $LE$ with generator $Li$. The sheafified-free universal property gives the same property to $(LB)[LE]$. Its normalized-realization clause supplies the unique $p:L(B[E])\cong(LB)[LE]$ with $pLi=j$: its inverse $q$ satisfies $qj=Li$, and $pq$ and $qp$ are identities since they fix the respective generators. All hypotheses are exactly the given small sites, left-exact adjunction and transported module operations. In Lean, remove the harmless ULift via the explicit rawLift isomorphism, apply freeModule_unique_iso to the transported restriction bijections supplied by geometricFreeModule_hom_chain, and translate the generator equation back. The seven unchanged free-sheaf constructions are now in their shared definition module [def-trf-free-module-sheaf-construction].

source.place: Tag 08TQ, lemma-pullback-differentials, free-module identifications; assembly of the re-split universal-property, transported-Hom and coherence lemmas.

proof.text: Apply the comparison-calculus lemma to $L$ and these $p$, for all coefficient sheaves and generator sheaves. Its representing-property hypothesis is the transported Hom bijection, and normalization is step 1. For $b:B\to B_1$ and $u:E\to E_1$, it gives $p_{B_1,E_1}L(c(b,u))=c(Lb,Lu)p_{B,E}$. Taking $b$ or $u$ to be an identity proves the two naturality clauses, with coefficient changes interpreted as semilinear maps.

proof.text: Apply freeModule_restrict_naturality to the identity module morphism and remove the underlying ULift to obtain generator naturality for the free functor. Compose the given normalization hp with the free functor applied to piComparison. This proves exactly the asserted product generator equation, including an empty index type; no product decomposition of free modules is used.

proof.text: For identity transport, use moduleAdd and moduleSMul on the sheaves of pairs of generalized operands to lift moduleUnderlying.inv to a linear module morphism; hB makes its coefficient map the identity. Compose with p.hom. The restriction bijection for the free module identifies this endomorphism with identity using hp. For composition, apply normalizedFreeModule_composition to f.inverse and g.inverse, and supply its transported representing hypothesis using geometricFreeModule_hom_chain for g.comp f. Its comparison maps are definitionally the comparisons in this module.
